See driverless tech in action at Autonomy Zone

Farm Progress Show: The Autonomy Zone offers farmers a hands-on look at robotic tractors and grain carts that could transform their operations.

Andy Castillo,Editor of Farm Equipment and Machinery,Farm ProgressAugust 27, 2026

schedule2 Min Read

Farmers can see autonomous equipment in action at the Farm Progress Show's Autonomy Zone from Sept. 1-3 in Boone, Iowa. Andy Castillo

Editor’s note: The Farm Progress Show will be Sept. 1-3 in Boone, Iowa. Visit FarmProgressShow.com.

A century ago, recently developed tractors were all the rage. Farmers across the country stood at field edges watching their neighbors’ machines chug around turnrows, wondering if it was the right time to invest.

Today’s autonomous technology is a lot more complex, but the overarching question is the same: When will it be financially viable? The Farm Progress Show’s Autonomy Zone is a place to find answers.

“Every year, Farm Progress is about finding what’s next. The Autonomy Zone is significant because it gives farmers a place to see autonomy in action — machines that think, adapt and lighten the workload,” said Rick Wild, operations manager and on-site show manager for the Farm Progress Show. “It’s where producers discover technology answers that can transform their operations today and define their competitive edge tomorrow.”

Related:How to avoid lines and find the perfect meal

Where to find it

Situated near the show’s field demonstration area, where harvest and tillage tools toil in front of crowds, and the Drone Zone, the Autonomy Zone will showcase robotic machines large and small — including driverless tractors pulling implements and autonomous grain cart operations.

Agricultural autonomy is in its infancy. Robotic machines operating on farms are still a relatively rare sight, let alone a chance to kick the tires and operate them from a tablet.

“We will create a dedicated Autonomy Zone — clearly marked, flagged off and built like a live demonstration,” Wild said. “It gives farmers a front‑row look at autonomous equipment operating with precision.”

Brand reps will be on hand to answer questions about the more technical aspects of autonomous operation, financial payback and their in-field capability. Numerous manufacturers will be on hand to demonstrate their machines.

The Autonomy Zone, which runs from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. daily in the show’s far northeastern corner, can be found outside the showground gates, “in the same area as the Ride and Drive,” Wild said.

“If you go straight out Gate 3 like you're heading toward the field demos and tram loading, the Autonomy Zone will be in that field,” he added.

There won’t be a regular schedule dictating when machines are demonstrated. Instead, brand experts will showcase them based on interest, either coordinating demonstrations at the Autonomy Zone area or at vendor booths within the grounds.

Prepare for demo areas

As veteran Farm Progress Show visitors know, venturing beyond the gates to the demonstration areas requires preparation. It’s a good idea to bunch stops together, visiting multiple outdoor areas in one trip. There will be a water station at the Gate 3 tram loading area.

Related:Feast on these food gems at 2026 Farm Progress Show

As always, check the weather and the Farm Progress Show app for updated information before heading out.

“Safety comes first,” Wild said. “If weather forces us to pause or close any demonstrations, updates will be pushed immediately through our digital channels and posted across the grounds. We’re committed to giving it to [attendees] the moment conditions shift.”

About the Author

Andy Castillo

Editor of Farm Equipment and Machinery, Farm Progress

Andy Castillo started his career in journalism about a decade ago as a television news cameraperson and producer before transitioning to a regional newspaper covering western Massachusetts, where he wrote about local farming. Between military deployments with the Air Force and covering the news, he earned an MFA in creative nonfiction writing from Bay Path University, building on the English degree he earned from the University of Massachusetts Amherst. In his role at Farm Progress, Castillo covers agricultural technology, new machinery and the constantly evolving farm equipment marketplace.

Castillo splits his time between the open road and western Massachusetts with his wife, Brianna, a travel nurse who specializes in pediatric oncology, and their rescue pup, Rio. When not attending farm shows, Castillo enjoys playing music, snowboarding, writing, cooking and restoring their 1920 craftsman bungalow. You can find Castillo at farm machinery shows across the country.

translationZh:
一个世纪前，新研发的拖拉机风靡一时。全国各地的农民站在田边，看着邻居的机器在地头转弯处轰鸣前行，心中思忖着是否到了投资的好时机。

如今的自主技术要复杂得多，但核心问题如出一辙：何时才能在财务上实现盈利？农场进步展的“自主作业区”正是寻找答案的地方。

“每一年，农场进步展都致力于发现前沿事物。自主作业区意义重大，因为它为农民提供了一个亲眼目睹自主技术实际运行的机会——这些机器能够思考、适应并减轻劳动负担，”农场进步展运营经理兼现场经理里克·怀尔德表示。“这里是生产者发现技术答案的地方，这些答案既能改变他们当下的运营方式，也能定义他们未来的竞争优势。”

**展区位置**

自主作业区位于展会现场演示区（收割和耕作工具在人群前作业）及无人机区附近，将展示大大小小的机器人设备——包括牵引农具的无人驾驶拖拉机以及自主谷物运输车作业。

农业自主技术尚处于起步阶段。在农场运行的机器人设备仍相对罕见，更不用说有机会亲手操作或通过平板电脑进行控制了。

“我们将打造一个专属的自主作业区——标识清晰、围栏明确，以现场演示的形式呈现，”怀尔德说。“它让农民能够前排观看自主设备精准作业。”

品牌代表将现场解答有关自主操作技术细节、投资回报及田间作业能力的问题。众多制造商将到场演示其设备。

自主作业区位于展会东北角最远端，每日上午10点至下午3点开放，展区位于展会大门外，“与试乘试驾区域在同一区域，”怀尔德说。

“如果你从3号门直行，就像前往田间演示区和摆渡车登车点那样，自主作业区就在那片田地里，”他补充道。

设备演示没有固定的时间表。品牌专家将根据观众兴趣进行展示，要么在自主作业区协调演示，要么在展场内的展商展位上进行。

**演示区准备提示**

农场进步展的资深观众都知道，走出大门前往演示区需要做好准备。建议将多个室外区域的参观合并安排，一次出行集中走访。3号门摆渡车登车点设有饮水站。

一如既往，出发前请查看天气预报和农场进步展官方应用程序以获取最新信息。

“安全第一，”怀尔德说。“如果天气原因迫使我们需要暂停或关闭任何演示，我们将通过数字渠道立即推送更新，并在展场各处张贴通知。我们致力于在天气条件变化的第一时间告知观众。”
